title: White Australia

draft.title: White Australia
card: The Immigration Restriction Act 1901 was one of the first laws passed by the new Australian Parliament after Federation. It was the main law behind the White Australia policy.
The Act did not name any race. Instead it gave officials the power to give a dictation test to a person who wanted to enter. The test could be set in any European language, chosen by the officer.
Officers could pick a language the person did not know, so most non-European migrants failed and were kept out. People from Europe were rarely tested.
The policy rested on racist beliefs and on fears about jobs and wages. It shaped who could migrate to Australia for decades, and its main parts ended in the 1960s and 1970s.
draft.remember: The 1901 Act used a dictation test to keep most non-European migrants out.

a.q: How did the Immigration Restriction Act 1901 keep most non-European migrants out without naming any race?
opts: It used a dictation test in a language chosen by the officer
It banned all ships from Asia from Australian ports
It set a limit on the number of migrants from each country
It required every migrant to own land in Australia
a.why: Officials could set the test in any European language, so they could make sure certain people failed. A ban on ships is wrong because the Act worked through testing individual people, not through closing ports.
a.clue: Think about the test officers could give to a person arriving.

b.q: In 1905, an officer gives Wen, a man from China, a dictation test in Dutch. Wen does not know Dutch. Why does this show the Act worked as a tool of exclusion?
opts: The officer could choose a language Wen would fail
The test measured whether Wen could read English
The test was only given to people who had a criminal record
The test was fair because every migrant sat it in Dutch
b.why: The officer chose the language, so the test could be made impossible to pass. It did not check English, because it could be set in any European language, and it was not given equally to all migrants.
b.clue: Who decided which language to use?

a.best: It used a dictation test in a language chosen by the officer

b.best: The officer could choose a language Wen would fail

problems.detail: The clue ('Think about the test officers could give') gives the answer away: only one option mentions a test, so a student can pick it without knowing the idea.
The clue ('Who decided which language to use?') points straight to the only option about the officer choosing the language, so the answer is given away.

proposal.title: White Australia
card: The Immigration Restriction Act 1901 was one of the first laws passed by the new Australian Parliament after Federation. It was the main law behind the White Australia policy.
The Act did not name any race. Instead it gave officials the power to give a dictation test to a person who wanted to enter. The test could be set in any European language, chosen by the officer.
Officers could pick a language the person did not know, so most non-European migrants failed and were kept out. People from Europe were rarely tested.
The policy rested on racist beliefs and on fears about jobs and wages. It shaped who could migrate to Australia for decades, and its main parts ended in the 1960s and 1970s.
proposal.remember: The 1901 Act used a dictation test to keep most non-European migrants out.

a.q: How did the Immigration Restriction Act 1901 keep most non-European migrants out without naming any race?
opts: A dictation test in a language chosen by the officer
An English reading test that every migrant had to pass
A yearly limit on the number of migrants from each country
An entry fee charged to every migrant arriving by ship
a.why: Officials could set the test in any European language, so they could make sure certain people failed. An English test sat by every migrant is wrong: the language was not fixed, and people from Europe were rarely tested at all.
a.clue: Think about how a rule could look fair yet still exclude people.

b.q: In 1903, an officer gives Wen, a man from China, a dictation test in Dutch. Wen does not know Dutch. Why does this show the Act worked as a tool of exclusion?
opts: The officer could choose a language Wen would fail
The test measured whether Wen could read English
The test was only given to people with a criminal record
The test was fair because every migrant sat it in Dutch
b.why: The officer chose the language, so the test could be made impossible to pass. It did not check English, because it could be set in any European language, and it was not given equally to all migrants.
b.clue: Ask whether Wen had any real chance to pass.
